key_headlines.summary: South Korea's National Assembly is expected to finalize electric vehicle tax credit policies by month-end, with government competitive strengthening measures imminent. Chinese EVs are surging with over 124,954 units imported in January-October, potentially exceeding nine years of cumulative imports.

key_headlines.summary: November consumer psychology index fell 2.3 points month-over-month due to stock market fluctuations and increased loan rates. Export gap between large corporations and SMEs has widened despite celebrating '1 trillion dollar exports' milestone.

key_headlines.title: Long-Term Inflation Pressures Persist as Bond Yields Remain High Despite Falling Oil Prices
key_headlines.summary: Government bond yields have decoupled from recent oil price declines, maintaining elevated levels due to lingering inflation pressures from prolonged high oil prices. Core inflation remains difficult to control, creating uncertainty about central bank rate-cut easing.

key_headlines.title: Trump Announces Ban on US Companies' Overseas Data Centers with Threat of Tax Penalties

key_headlines.title: Samsung Electronics Promotes 131 Executives, Prioritizing Semiconductor and AI Talent
key_headlines.summary: Samsung promoted 131 executives including 39 vice presidents, with 53% from semiconductor division, reflecting record performance. Key promotions went to HBM-4 and robotics talent, with female promotions reaching historic high of 11.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's economy faces mounting pressures from persistent inflation and consumer sentiment deterioration despite export growth. The consumer sentiment index fell to a 7-month low of 103.1 in November, declining 2.3 points due to stock market volatility and rising interest rates. While semiconductor and shipbuilding sectors show strength, automotive and petrochemical industries face headwinds, and the gap between large corporations and SMEs in exports is widening. Electric vehicle tax credit policies are expected to be finalized this week amid mounting pressure from Chinese EV competition, which surged to 124,954 units in January-October alone.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: Bond market participants anticipate a base rate hike by the Bank of Korea in November, with 54% expecting increases amid persistent inflation concerns and expectations for US Federal Reserve rate hikes in December. Goldman Sachs forecasts the Korean won-to-dollar rate at 1,280 won next year, with predictions that Korea's base rate will struggle to exceed 3.5% due to limited room for tightening amid semiconductor export strength. The persistence of core inflation and domestic credit growth, combined with anticipated US Federal Reserve tightening, constrains the central bank's policy flexibility despite economic headwinds.
sections.Financial Markets: The KOSPI regained the 5,000 level following CEO Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia, with the index surging over 6% as semiconductor stocks led the rally and foreign investors returned as buyers. Bond yields showed mixed movements across maturities, while the won-dollar exchange rate declined only 3.5 won despite KOSPI gains, constrained by divergent dollar supply-demand from stock trading and persistent global dollar strength. Taiwan's stock market hit record highs with a 9.15% surge, buoyed by optimism surrounding semiconductor sector recovery.
sections.Industry & Technology: Samsung Electronics promoted 131 executives in its regular appointment, with 53% from the semiconductor division led by HBM-4 developers and AI-robotics talent, reflecting record-breaking performance this year. LG Energy Solution is implementing comprehensive battery lifecycle management from production through reuse in energy storage systems, supporting Korea's energy transition goals. Industry forecasts predict 14% export growth to $1.3 trillion next year, with semiconductors accounting for 50% of exports, while non-semiconductor sectors like automobiles and petrochemicals face stagnation, intensifying K-shaped economic polarization.
sections.Real Estate: Housing price expectations fell by 6 points month-over-month to 118, marking the sharpest decline in eight months as consumer sentiment deteriorated, while apartment deposits remain increasingly inaccessible for younger generations despite falling purchase prices. Redevelopment concerns persist as the gap between sale prices and rental availability widens, with young people citing affordability crises similar to European cities. New construction apartments in provincial areas show signs of recovery, with new pre-lease apartments drawing over 100 waiting teams despite freezing temperatures.
sections.International Economy: Trump's administration is considering overproduction tariffs targeting China and the EU, with exclusions for automobiles, steel, and aluminum under existing trade laws, potentially affecting Korean exporters. The Federal Reserve faces scrutiny over communication protocols as Deputy Chair Bowman attended a Wall Street dinner hours after announcing rate decisions, violating blackout period guidelines. Copper prices have plummeted as a leading indicator of US economic slowdown, with Atlanta Federal Reserve GDP Now model estimating Q4 growth at 3.2%, below Q3's 3.4% preliminary figure.
sections.AI & Economy: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Powell warned that AI investment returns failing to meet expectations could trigger stock declines and significant economic slowdown with rising unemployment, raising concerns about circular financing risks. Hanwha Aerospace is constructing a 180-megawatt defense AI data center with initial 10 trillion won investment, transforming Korea's defense industry from hardware-focused weapons systems to AI-based integrated solutions. Optical fiber prices have surged sevenfold due to drone usage in conflicts, threatening critical AI industry supply chains, while anticipated US-China trade conflict escalation in January could further restrict access to advanced semiconductors and minerals.
sections.Others: Government industrial policy faces criticism for encouraging unfair practices, with regulations penalizing business expansion and job creation through extended work-hour restrictions for companies with five or more employees. US law enforcement is tightening financial channels for North Korea's nuclear and WMD development funding following failed North America dialogue prospects, targeting illegal foreign currency acquisition schemes. Memory semiconductor demand remains resilient with long-term contracts providing underlying support, according to US semiconductor investment strategists, suggesting computing power remains in short supply despite regulatory headwinds.
